source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #357 (branch fix/320-resource-validation at head 3ec45760193cfa608c075230c4f46706dc8c1ff5 — the #320 change with its three Codex P2 fixes (a sub-ascribed type export registers its fresh face identity in the type index and export info; the export (sub resource) ascription check accepts abstract resource faces; and export (eq ...) ascriptions over resource faces require nominal identity), on current main 98e93a3 (PR #349); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45626770085, 45626777366 and 45626784798 against the branch and pull-request run 45625724782, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #357’s Codex round-3 fix (nominal identity for export eq ascriptions over resource faces). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45626794894, 45626804707 and 45626813591 on main at 98e93a3; all three runs pass the gate). The main control reproduces the checked-in baseline byte-identically on the 24 series of the baseline and telomere-component-linking configurations and sits slightly below it on the eight core-only series (by 256–512 B stripped file and 144–320 B stripped .text — pre-existing baseline staleness; no core series is re-baselined, as the branch is byte-identical to the main control there). This PR’s own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +5,184 B (component), +5,200 B (wasi) and +5,200 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +4,688 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +4,032 B / +4,032 B / +4,016 B and stripped .text +3,520 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline (by +1,752–+1,784 B stripped file and +1,648 B stripped .text in release; by +1,808 B and +1,680 B in release-size), so those twelve are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.64% (2,433,656 B to 2,716,832 B); the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
